A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SleepLM study. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–E are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, figures, tables, and examples can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on sleep classification, regression, retrieval, captioning, transfer learning, and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds CFS comparisons with specialized models and explicit caption-generation scores.

M1.justification: The captioning pipeline, ReCoCa architecture, modality conditioning, and contrastive, reconstruction, and captioning objectives are unchanged. The added downstream evaluations do not introduce a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use SHHS, MrOS, CCSHS, CFS, and WSC and retain the same physiological tasks. The new CFS adaptation experiments reuse already covered data and classification targets under different evaluation procedures. Newly disclosed demographics do not establish a changed population.

E2.justification: v2 adds actual comparisons against RobustSleepNet, U-Sleep, SleepFM, and Chronos-2 in Tables 13–14. This substantially expands the comparator set beyond the retained general SSL, supervised, LLM, and VLM baselines to specialized sleep models and a time-series foundation model.

E3.justification: The original frozen-encoder WSC evaluation at 1–50 shots is retained. Appendix D.4 adds CFS evaluation with 10-shot and 50-shot linear probing and full fine-tuning, reporting AUC on its test split. It specifies shared pretraining splits for sleep models and use of Chronos-2's public checkpoint. These introduce substantial additional evaluation designs.

E4.justification: The reconstruction and caption ablations, model/data scaling studies, timestamp perturbations, embedding analyses, retrieval examples, and full-night case study are retained. The new domain-model comparisons and caption scores are additional benchmark results, without new ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the reported comparisons. The added tables continue point-estimate reporting. Disclosure of 930 validation participants concerns sample composition, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results remain unchanged, but Tables 13–14 add substantial CFS results. SleepLM leads all four 50-shot tasks; with full fine-tuning, Chronos-2 leads sleep staging (87.6 versus 87.2 AUC) and hypopnea (85.0 versus 83.0). Table 20 adds explicit caption scores, including SleepLM's 91.8 BERTF1 and 44.2 METEOR, beyond v1's Figure 1 overview. Table 6 adds age proportions. These are additional results, not demonstrated performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and associated definitions are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the sleep-text dataset, ReCoCa, language-grounded sleep understanding, and unseen-concept capabilities. The added comparisons support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4 newly attributes foundation models' comparative strengths partly to parameter scale and transferable representations, discussing Chronos-2's strong fine-tuning performance. Table 6 interprets the older demographic skew as consistent with clinical prevalence. The stated clinical-validation and cohort-coverage limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly discloses 930 validation participants: 409 SHHS, 193 MrOS, and 328 CFS, alongside age distributions. Appendix D.4 describes baseline pretraining alignment and Chronos-2 checkpoint use. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing, prompts, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to RobustSleepNet, Hearts, and OSF and removes CoSleep. Previously cited SleepFM, U-Sleep, and Chronos-2 also gain explicit experimental comparison roles. The related-work narrative and central novelty positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: Localized expansions appear in Sections 5.1, B.1, and D.4, with a new caption-score subsection D.11 and acknowledgments. Minor wording and cross-reference edits accompany them. The main organization and most prose, including Appendix E's examples and prompts, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds demographic Table 6, comparison Tables 13–14, and caption-score Table 20, with localized figure/table relocation and text reflow. The full-night table corrects CoCa labels to ReCoCa while retaining its values. Existing figures and the overall visual design are preserved.

improvement.justification: The specialized-model comparisons improve the empirical context, while demographic disclosure and explicit caption scores improve transparency. These gains are limited by incomplete specification of the new CFS adaptation protocol and absent uncertainty estimates. Section 5.1's claim of consistently matching or exceeding domain-specific methods also overstates Tables 13–14, which show clear exceptions. Overall, the revision provides a useful but bounded quality improvement.
